intended_object: The degree shift M{n} of a ℤ-graded module M over a graded algebra (𝒜): the same underlying A-module, regraded by (M{n})_p = M_{p−n}. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition keeps the carrier and its module structures and takes the grading `M.grading.shift (-n)`. `InternalGrading.shift G c` has p-th piece `G.piece (p + c)`, so the p-th piece of `M{n}` is `M_{p-n}`, which is exactly what the docstring says. The proof of `gradedSMul` checks that 𝒜_i · M_{j-n} ⊆ M_{i+j-n}, which is the compatibility a graded module needs. The sign convention (M{1})_p = M_{p-1} is a standard one, and the module documentation states it explicitly. The setting is the library's own category `GradedModuleCat 𝒜`, which is generic over a commutative ring k and a k-algebra A. Mathlib has no bundled category of graded modules with a shift, so there is no more general version that the definition fails to use.
